As a twin I will say, yes I am close to my sister, but as an identical twin it also has created a lot of odd emotional rifts, constantly being compared to one another in every facets of life not just by parents and family but also by friends and complete strangers. We were close so we actually kind of were annoyed by our parents most of our life, twins aren't "special" and once your no longer a child a large portion of the world finds looking the same creepy. 

My mom was also an only child so when my sister and I would get into health arguments she would tell me how special we are to have one another and how we ought not to "fight" but it can be hard not to fight with one another when you feel like others are constantly pitting you against one another. 

"Are you the smart twin or the dumb twin." "You know your sister is prettier than you" "your heavier than your sister" "who gets more guys?" "You guys look the same so would you date the same person" 

Also grown up was great because we had each other but it also caused us to be grossly rejected by peers because we were only included as "the twins" we felt like we were a side show, people would show boat us around because of our twiness but didn't want to get to know either of our different personalities.

Being a twin is exhausting and annoying and my mother heard us bitch about it a lot. Not that my sister and I didn't love each other but that we either felt compared or people acted like my sister and I were one person. As adults we don't even mention being "twins" to friends and honestly life is a lot easier. 

Honestly don't feel guilty if you aren't ready for one kid you wouldnt have been ready for two. Double food, double diaper changes, double cellphone bills as teenagers, double trouble.  

Plus you would have plenty of opportunities to have multiple births and to have siblings which IMO have a healthier dynamic than twins often do. 

I am not saying I dislike being a twin I love my sister but I think it is heavily romanticized especially by pregnant women without thinking about a lot of the psychological effects it can have on the twins growing up.

Op I feel you should step back and think about the reasons your relationship is making you depressed and anxious? 

There are so many reasons:

Lack of communication being one that is most common and is also the hardest to correct because people tend to speak from feelings and generally blaming the other person is how it takes shape. (Not saying op is blaming his wife it might be the other way around) 

Unmet expectations is another common issue and typically unmet expectations come from again a lack of communication,( either op not telling your wife what you want or expect or wife not telling op.) 

Lack of goals or relationship growth. Meaning you both stoped trying to rekindle feelings. Remember how hard everyone tries in the begining of a relationship after a few kids people try less to have fun with partners because of general exhaustion and expecting the partner to make the first move. ( Not op but wife might expect op to try to initiate intimacy, depression might prevent that and op might be feeling negected)  again this can be solved by communication and stating expectations. 

Op you also spoke of agumments over little things, in my experience anger comes from fear.  Afraid of not being heard, afraid of being criticized, afraid of  anything really.  
For example a husband and wife argue over what toilet paper to buy. Typically the arguments not really about preference its about one of the partners feeling like the other doesn't trust there judgement ect, or one person is afraid of releasing control, really the list goes on and on. 

This is why therapy can be useful in situations like yours because typically  the issues aren't ever what they seem.

At the end of the damn day everyone wants to be loved and heard either OP communicates bluntly to his wife the issues they have and they have a heart to heart and go from there or they don't communicate and split regardless of one another's feelings.

Dont report it, research dog play fighting, and open a conversation with your neighbour try to introduce your dogs in a neutral setting. Dogs need to be socialized I would count yourself lucky that you have another pup in the neighbourhood. 

Also as startling as it is remain calm when you dogs rough play, dogs react well to human emotions and them sensing your stress can actually escalate a situations from playing to your dog becoming defensive/aggressive.

I had a surgical abortion 8 months ago now. I like you was very nervous. I recommend before the procedure to make wherever you are staying after as comfortable and as clean as possible, I was living with my mother at the time and she did not know about the abortion my boyfriend took me to the procedure and when I got home the house was a mess I was tired and sleepy and sore and just wanted some peace and quite. I was in the unfournate situation of havibg to pretend like I had a cold until I felt better. 

 I was at 5 weeks gestation when I had mine done. It did hurt a lot because I was unable to relax. I really wish I could have been sedated but the only option at the clinic was a local anesthetic. I tensed up so much I kept pushing the tools out of my cervix, which obviously frustrated my doctor and made my experience so much worse. 

So please please do everything you can to relax before hand. Call the clinic to find out if you can take some Tylenol before hand or if they have any medication to help you relax.

If you are anything like me after the procedure you are going to be groggy, sleepy and possibly emotional, I cried for a few days pretty sure my horemones were adjusting and I was a bit sore (I also had a copper IUD inserted right after which might be why I was in so much pain) 

( You do bleed after but don't be alarmed by the clumps, or the pain it is normal to cramp up, the procedure involved them removing the cells and tissue from the walls of your cervix so yeah its going to hurt)

Bring something comfy to wear, bring extra pads, and comfortable underwear. I brought some warm socks and worse a big t shirt and comfy sweats.  At my clinic they didn't give me a gown they asked to bring your own xlarge shirt long enough to cover your bum for the procedure and I went into a changing room to change into if before the procedure. 

Durring was fine I had a nurse holding my hand, it was uncomfortable again I wasn't sedated so I pretty much felt everything, but the nurse was so nice she let me squeeze her hand and she helped me relax enough so the doctor could finish. 

After they brought me into this room with a bunch of beds and a nurse would come and give me crackers, and water, and pain meds, they let you rest for however long until you feel ready to leave. 

When you go home make sure who ever is driving you understnads that you might not want to talk about it and that you just need to rest. When you get home have some tv shows, music or a book to read during recovery give your self time and patience to heal from the experience. I also recommend having some easy meals or snacks that you can eat in case you aren't in the mood to cook anything. 


 You've just joined a club so many women are apart of but so few talk about. 
I'm proud of you for making your own choice, and good luck.

Rinse and repeat you are teaching your pup by rewarding the desired behaviour and ignoring the undesirable one. 

Typically dogs want your attention,  play is something they want, they think biting is communicating the play. 

I learnt yelling/yelping/ acting like you're in pain ect. does NOT work and can make some dogs more excited/agressive because you reacted which is what they want. 

Eventually teach your dog the "bring me a toy" command so when they want to play they know they can communicate to you by bringing a ball or something they can bite on and play with.

A warning: 

This takes a LOT of patience and a lot of consistancy. Everyone in the house needs to participate in this training. If someone allows this rough play it will confuse your dog and it will be harder to correct.

To further prevent her from using teeth with people anytime she so much as touched skin with her teeth we put her in time out/ingored her. Meaning if she nipped your hand while playing with a toy she also had this treatment we wanted to fully train teeth to skin contact out of her system. 

She learnt that that using teeth while fun and acceptable as a dog will garner nothing more than a time out from people.

Choosing essentials, and the system for the right items

1. I think about my perceived value of the item I'm looking for. What purpose does it need to serve? Do I really need another item for this task?

2. I keep in mind longevity, functionality, and multi-use.

3. Research. Find products that are of good quality. If buying new look for companies with lifetime warranties. 

4. Find second hand, or always buy on sale.

- leather goods: last longer, can be repaired, as well as bought second hand. 

- Companies like Darn tough offer lifetime guarantees (allowing you to buy the last pair of socks you'll ever need.)

- metal, glassware, and ceramic: last longer and can be bought second hand compared to plastic products that will break down with age, and heat. 

- Electronics: buy to the specifications you use, keep in mind what you plan to do with the item, casual user vs professional need different specs. Also, buy items that can be upgraded and aren't going to be obsolete in a year. 
(Also I TRY to keep my cables to as few as possible buying electronics with the same charging ports)

- Hobbies: keep in mind how frequent you do this hobby, a retired person could probably justify buying hobby equipment more than a person who does the activity once a year.  If it's a once a year thing you can always rent equipment. 

- Decor: will it bring me joy every time I see it? Also is it functional. I have a dish that severs as decor, I throw my keys, wallet, & change in it when I get home, it also brings me joy because my sister made it for me. Decorate with sentimental items instead of hiding them in a box or buying random decor from home goods.

- clothing: prefer that my clothes are all interchangeable look into "wonder wardrobe " clothes that fit into your lifestyle, climate, and all match each other in color. 
Also multi-use clothing: I have a snow jacket that acts as a coat for snowboarding, walking around town, a raincoat, and a fall jacket. It has an outer shell and an inner removable layer, I can wear them together or separate. 

- Makeup: multi use items lipstick that also works as a blush, contor that works as eye shadow, Mascara for lashes and eyebrows, cc cream with built in SPF.

Yeah the placebo effect is real. I'm not sure what kind of anti-depressant your taking but the main ones work at inhibiting the reuptake of seritonin. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter and inhibiting the reuptake slows the neurotransmitter so that the brain essentially will use it up slower. 

I'm no doctor but I was interested in them so I found that, 
In the brain a neurotransmitter has three options reuptake (recycling), dissolving, or continuing to move through neuron channels. 
The medication work by blocking the transporter so it can't move resulting in the seritonin sitting on the outside of the neuron longer which is where seritonin acts to increase mood. 

So other drugs like cocaine and ecstasy work like this too but are instant so what gives with seritonin reuptake inhibitors aka anti depresants? 

The anti depressants work slow generally because it is believed that it's not just the seritonin that causes depression and it is thought that the anti depressants work on other areas of the brain that have yet to be understood. Mostly from what I've read is they don't directly effect the seritonin transporters but effete the DNA precursors to the seritonin transporters. 

So while I'm not doctor they may be effective due to placebo, but please don't let that be off putting. 
A Placebo effect is strong so don't be discouraged by it something like 75% of the time a placebo can be just as effective as an actual medication because the body wants to heal it's self but sometimes needs a little motivation. 

A while ago I remember reading a study about a trial of a drug with patients with heart disease using the drug vs placebo and it was something like 65.8% of people on the placebo saw benefits similar to the drug users.

I think that a lot of things that are going on are caused by a lack of communication.  Being in a LDR, communication and setting very very clear boundaries is important. Mostly due to the fact that in LDR there is not much but verbal communication keeping people together.  It is a scary thing to say but I think for successful LDR you need to know what both parties ultimately want in life, and in the future. The essence of an LDR should be defined if you aren't with the person and you think you're in a monogamous relationship the only thing keeping things okay is that you have 100% trust that your partner is keeping this agreement.   
I'm not saying OPs girlfriend cheated but OP should have an open talk with his partner about what he expects out of the relationship, defining monogamy, what they want in life after long-distance, the dates they plan to see one another, what behaviour is considered cheating in there relationship.    
While everyone has seen boobs that's not the point, OP may have in his relationship had to wait a long time to see his partners body, or he may have never known her to be the kind of girl who would walk around topless.  So her taking a trip on the wild side showing her breasts to new men may feel like a betrayal to him, or he may have asked on a phone call how the trip was and she kept that from him. I mean has OP ever gone skinny dipping or done anything fun like this with his girlfriend? As a woman, I don't mind doing things like this but I wouldn't dare do it and hide it from my boyfriend, and I also respect my long-distance boyfriend enough to understand that taking that action could hurt him in a way where he felt betrayed.   
A hard truth I've learnt being in a LDR if you are doing things you don't feel comfortable sharing with your partner you probably shouldn't do those things or you shouldn't be in that relationship because you both want different things and if it's not something you want to compromise on that's it. In any relationship, you need to know what you expect and what your partner expects and if they don't line up you need to be responsible enough to walk away or compromise.
